findings.location: docs/CODEX_SETUP.md:69-74 (section 2, the curl and PowerShell installers paragraph)
findings.evidence: NON-BLOCKING. The coordinator's copies <S>/codex-install.sh and <S>/codex-install.ps1 are byte-identical to the 2026-10-05 fetches in qa-786x-r1 (`cmp`, rc=0 for both). install.sh: line 5 `RELEASE="${CODEX_RELEASE:-latest}"`, line 86 `--release)`, line 83 `parse_args()`, line 1080 `parse_args "$@"`. install.ps1, lines 2-3: `param([string]$Release = $env:CODEX_RELEASE)`.
findings.description: The cited source facts are right, and R1-F3 is resolved. The section names flags rather than invocations, and each common one-liner has a trap. In `curl ... | sh`, the variable must prefix `sh` (`curl -fsSL https://chatgpt.com/codex/install.sh | CODEX_RELEASE=0.145.0 sh`), and the flag needs `sh -s -- --release 0.145.0`. Prefixing curl instead silently installs the newest release. In PowerShell's `irm ... | iex` form, `-Release` cannot be bound, but `$env:CODEX_RELEASE='0.145.0'` can, because the param default reads it. The section's own `codex --version` check would catch a mis-pinned install, and it states that only npm was verified, so this is info only.
